data.name: Mold on the Pizza
data.detailed_description:
Warning!

Don’t take this game lightly—just by looking at its cute characters! :)

Key Features

* Offense & strategy game

* 53 types of cute characters

* 192 stages

* 8 kinds of mini-games

* Complete support for game pad

* Local Cooperation, PvP, AI modes

* 36 achievements

Story

A cute mold named "Pang" is in love with a pizza. Floating in the air, Pang recognized the inviting smell of a pizza and rushed toward it right away. But what he found there along with a pizza were heaps of preservative troops that fight mold.

With Pang’s arrival on the pizza, preservatives began to attack him!

Pang grew furious – and soon he decided to gather all his friends and eat the pizza!

Here now, Pang and his friends need your help to defeat preservative troops and occupy a pizza!

Mold

Create 21 different types of mold to occupy a pizza!

Preservatives

Fight 32 different types of preservatives that prevent mold from occupying a pizza, destroy a building and get droplets to create more mold!

Pickle

Pickles are granted after clearing every stage. Bring them to the lab for upgrades into even more powerful troops!

Topping Slots

Get slots from each theme after clearing every stage. Equip a mold with slots and make it more powerful!

Bosses

Slay the preservative boss waiting for you at the end of each theme and occupy a pizza.

192 Stages

Select either regular or large level—each level consists of eight themes, each of which has 12 stages. Experience different types of battles across 192 stages!

Mini games

8 kinds of mini-games will never leave you bored!

Local Co-op

Is the game too hard? Use a game pad to enjoy a co-op with friends (up to 4)! Get or give help from / to your friend(s)!

PvP

Enjoy a PvP online! Now battle players all over the world!

Also battle AI characters that keep evolving!

Use a game pad to enjoy a PvP with your friend. Now, try to win over your friend!

Achievements

Mold on the Pizza has 36 achievements!

Thanks for your interest and enjoy the game!

reviews.review:
Mold on the Pizza is one of those games where the idea sounds completely ridiculous until I actually start playing it. I am controlling little pieces of mold that are trying to take over a pizza while fighting against preservatives that are trying to stop me. The whole thing is presented with bright and silly characters, but underneath that there is a simple strategy game where I have to decide what mold to create, where to send it and when to spend my resources. I like how quickly it gets going because I do not have to sit through a huge introduction before I can start figuring things out for myself.

The main campaign has a surprising amount of content. There are 192 stages spread across eight different themes, with regular and large levels, and I get 21 different types of mold to use against 32 different types of preservatives. That gives me quite a few different units to experiment with, especially once I start unlocking stronger types and using the upgrades from completed stages. The toppings system also lets me improve my molds, so there is a little bit of progression alongside the actual strategy. For such a strange little free game, I was not expecting this much content.

What I like most is that the battles are simple but still give me things to think about. I have to spread my mold across the pizza, deal with enemy troops and destroy buildings so I can collect the droplets needed to create more mold. I cannot just keep producing units forever, so I have to pay attention to what is happening and make sure I am not wasting my resources. The different preservatives also force me to change what I am doing instead of using exactly the same group every time. The bosses at the end of each theme give the campaign a nice sense of progression too.

There are also a lot of extra things packed into the game. I get eight different mini games, along with local cooperative play for up to four people, PvP and battles against AI. I like having these options because they give me something else to do once I have had enough of the main campaign. The local co op is especially nice for a game this small because I can bring someone into a difficult stage and work through it together. The game also supports controllers properly, which makes the whole thing feel more complete than I expected from something that is completely free.

The biggest problem for me is that the game can become repetitive after a while. The basic idea does not really change that much, so even with all the different molds and preservatives I am still trying to take over sections of a pizza and keep the enemy from doing the same thing to me. Some of the later stages also feel like they are testing how well I understand the existing systems rather than introducing something completely new. I think that is fine for a strategy game built around repeating its core mechanics, but it stops the game from feeling as fresh after I have played a lot of it.

The presentation is another part I have mixed feelings about. I like the cute style and the ridiculous idea of a war between mold and preservatives, and the different pizza themed areas give the game plenty of character. At the same time, it clearly comes from an older free to play game design and some parts feel rough around the edges. The interface is functional rather than polished, and I sometimes feel like I am playing something that was designed more around having lots of content than making every part of the experience feel refined. I can forgive that because the game is free, but it is still noticeable.

Overall, Mold on the Pizza is much better than I expected from the name alone. I like the strange setting, the simple strategy, the huge number of stages and the surprisingly large selection of molds and enemies. The extra mini games and multiplayer options are also a nice bonus, although the basic gameplay can become repetitive once I have seen enough of it. It is definitely not the most polished strategy game I have played, but it has enough content and personality to make the free price feel almost irrelevant. For me, it is one of those weird little games that ends up being much more enjoyable than it has any right to be.

Rating: 7.8/10
